text:
pager-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 1725312345 - high kv_cache eviction + cont-batch queue depth spike for model-group:gqa-mqa (hosts: rl-infer-eu-*) -- error_rate 5xx increased from 0.2% -> 6.8%, p95 latency from 120ms -> 620ms. link: https://metrics.redwood.internal/alerts/1725312345

jamal: oncall here, ack. I’m looking. @sana can you grab runtime? I see correlating prefetch/prefix blowouts for Llama and Mistral variants in the same shard set.

sana: looking. root cause likely kv cache cardinality explosion + continuous-batching holding many inflight prefixes (GQA paths) — cont-batch window grew to 250ms due to a bad adaptive policy, causing huge KV retention.\nWorking hypothesis: a recent rollout of adaptive-contbatch (beta) bumped window under high concurrency for qwen/mqa mix, magnifying prefix churn.

rika: tagging ML-eng: the affected traffic is primarily `gqa-mqa-v2` and `mistral-1.1-prefetch` families. MQA heavy requests with many short prefixes are amplifying KV footprint.

oliver: Customer Impact: one enterprise customer on EU region reported 30+ 5xx in the last 10m and chat sessions timing out. CS contacted them, they’ve disabled some high-verbosity features. We should prepare a brief notify.

jamal: immediate mitigation plan (live):
1) disable adaptive-contbatch for affected shard pool (rl-infer-eu-*)
2) reduce continuous_batch_window_ms from 250 -> 40 for cont-batching fallback
3) set kv_cache_prefetch=false for models: gqa-mqa-v2, mistral-prefetch variants
4) roll a targeted restart of the shard pool with no full rollout (canary first)

sana: I can patch runtime config now. executing hotfix command: ```
# runtime hotfix
rctl set pool rl-infer-eu-* adaptive_contbatch.enabled=false
rctl set pool rl-infer-eu-* continuous_batch_window_ms=40
rctl set model gqa-mqa-v2 kv_cache.prefetch=false
```

deploy-bot: starting job deploy/rl-hotfix-1725312345 -> canary on rl-infer-eu-01 (job id: dj-8241). Logs: https://deploys.redwood.internal/dj-8241

netops: note: if we restart too many pods at once we risk capacity loss; recommend serial canary then 5% parallel. I'll throttle the restart.

jamal: agreed. @deploy-bot kick canary, monitor p95/p99 and kv_evictions. If 3 consecutive canary checks pass (5m), proceed with 10% roll.

(5m later) deploy-bot: canary complete, checks: kv_eviction_rate down 72%, p95 latency down to 210ms, error_rate down to 1.1%. Proceeding with ramp to 10%.

oliver: reported customer just confirmed their chat load stabilized after 2 minutes of the canary changes. They ask for ETA on permanent fix.

rika: ML-eng action items: disable prefetch heuristics for MQA path in model config, add a guard in the model adapter to cap prefix cardinality per request, and add an eval to catch this pattern in CI.

jamal: oncall handoff: I’ll stay until full ramp (expected 30m) then hand to @rika for postmortem and long-term mitigation. Handoff summary: hotfix applied to rl-infer-eu-*, adaptive-contbatch disabled, cont_batch_window lowered, kv prefetch off for listed models. Customer impacted: EU-enterprise-42 saw 5xx/timeouts; currently stable.

rika: taking at 1725313600. I’ll kick off an incident ticket and assign owners: runtime (sana) for hotfix follow-up, ml-eng (rika) for model adapter changes, infra (netops) for safer restart plan, cs (oliver) for customer comm.

jamal: thumbs. postmortem checklist: timeline, config diff, root cause (adaptive algorithm + MQA cardinality), mitigation timeline, follow-ups (rate-limit prefix generation, add cont-batch backpressure, canary automation).

oliver: I’ll draft the customer note: brief incident summary, what we changed, ETA for permanent fix (TBD but aim EOD), and an offer for a post-incident call.

deploy-bot: full ramp to pool 100% complete at 1725313480. No regression alerts since.

rika: closing handoff. tag:incident-reviewed, assigning postmortem owner: rika. next: schedule retro with ML, runtime, SRE.

pager-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED 1725313600 - service metrics returned to baseline and customer reports restored. Close after postmortem filed. :white_check_mark:
